title: (Early) AI Compute Asset Pricing
key_claim: Compute capital expenditure and service flow already exceed 1% of US GDP; the announced launch of compute futures turns AI-adoption uncertainty into a tradable risk, but compute is non-storable, so storage-based no-arbitrage pricing fails and early evidence points to a positive compute risk premium driven by provider hedging pressure.
frame_summary: The paper argues compute is becoming a financialised asset class whose futures cannot be priced like storable commodities, and offers an early asset-pricing treatment with preliminary evidence of a positive compute risk premium.
verbatim_quote: Compute capital expenditure and service flow already exceed 1% of U.S. GDP and are growing rapidly.
verbatim_list: Compute capital expenditure and service flow already exceed 1% of U.S. GDP and are growing rapidly.
The announced launch of compute futures turns this uncertainty into a tradable risk, raising questions on the pricing of a new asset class.
In this respect, compute is closer to electricity, freight, or other capacity-constrained service commodities than to a storable physical commodity, such as oil or metals.
Our preliminary evidence is consistent with a positive compute risk premium, suggesting hedging pressure on the part of compute providers.

title: Financing the AI infrastructure boom: on- and off-balance sheet borrowing (BIS Quarterly Review box)
date_evidence: meta-DC.date: 2026-03-16 | visible dateline: BIS Quarterly Review | 16 March 2026
key_claim: Hyperscaler AI capex is increasingly debt-funded: gross corporate bond issuance topped $100 billion in 2025, and off-balance sheet SPV structures amount to shadow borrowing that links hyperscalers to private credit and creates new shock-transmission channels.
frame_summary: The BIS box argues the AI buildout's financing has shifted to leverage, on-balance-sheet through record bond issuance and off-balance-sheet through SPV lease structures that are economically debt but sit outside balance sheets.
verbatim_quote: Their gross issuance increased markedly, topping $100 billion in 2025
verbatim_list: Corporate bond markets have been hyperscalers' primary source of financing. Their gross issuance increased markedly, topping $100 billion in 2025
These arrangements amount to "shadow borrowing": obligations that are economically akin to debt but largely reside outside corporate balance sheets.

title: How Central Banks Can Contain Financial Stability Risks as AI Accelerates Change
key_claim: The IMF's Financial Counsellor calls on central banks and supervisors to map AI-related dependencies system-wide, set minimum resilience standards for critical providers, and improve visibility into AI use and concentration, because many AI applications rely on a small number of cloud, data or model providers.
frame_summary: Adrian argues AI is now a financial-stability issue and that authorities need stronger oversight, better data and deeper coordination, with concentration in a few critical compute and model providers a central systemic vulnerability.

title: ICE and Ornn to Launch GPU Compute Futures Contracts
date_evidence: ICE and Ornn to Launch GPU Compute Futures Contracts — dateline: May 19, 2026
key_claim: ICE and Ornn will launch US-dollar-denominated, cash-settled GPU compute futures referencing the transaction-based Ornn Compute Price Index across H100, H200, B200 and RTX 5090 hardware, subject to regulatory approval.
frame_summary: ICE and Ornn present compute as a trillion-dollar market lacking the pricing and risk-transfer infrastructure every other major commodity relies on, and position OCPI futures as that missing layer.
